source.title: Imperfect Segmentation Labels: How Much Do They Matter?
source.authors: N. Heller; Joshua Dean; N. Papanikolopoulos

record.tranche_reason: Tests how perturbed training labels affect segmentation performance, using different perturbations and Dice scores rather than the original random-label classification experiment.
record.gate_note: The study reports test Dice scores for three label-perturbation modes. It does not report training error, fitting time, unstructured inputs, explicit regularization, or learning order. Only the random-perturbation results bear on V4; boundary-localized perturbations are outside that version.
record.test_reason: The study tests V4's test-performance component in a new setting: liver segmentation with increasing random voxel-label corruption. It does not test whether networks memorize the corrupted training masks.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report general degradation with increasing boundary-localized errors, robustness to random voxel-label errors across all three architectures, and comparatively strong U-Net performance under large choppy perturbations. They do not conclude that the networks perfectly fit or memorize corrupted labels.
record.recipe_differences: Medical image segmentation with perturbed masks, rather than image classification with completely random image labels; reports test Dice, not training error or test error at chance.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture and perturbation mode; performance on random perturbations differs by model, and U-Net has anomalously good performance under large choppy perturbations.

fits_no_version.finding: Boundary-localized natural and choppy mask perturbations generally reduce test Dice; U-Net is comparatively robust to large choppy perturbations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Segmentation sensitivity to annotation errors depends on their spatial structure and the architecture.

record.problems: Single dataset with binary labels; no training-error or training-time results; five training runs per architecture and perturbation pair but no uncertainty values are shown in Table 1; limited tested corruption range.
record.rows_left_out: Rows for natural and choppy perturbations in Table 1 are not included because those conditions do not test V4's random-label-corruption condition.

untested.parts: Completely random training labels, zero or near-zero training error, chance-level test error, and fitting without changing architecture or training hyperparameters.
Time required to fit true versus random labels and convergence speed across corruption levels. A fixed 100-epoch training budget does not measure time to fit.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect fitting of corrupted training labels, memorization of noise, corruption extending to completely random labels, and test error approaching chance. Dice targets are mask-agreement levels, not reported fractions of corrupted labels.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noisy labels; no training trajectories or clean-versus-noisy learning-order measurements are reported.

record.verdict_notes: All recorded numerical values match Table 1. Random 0.95, 0.90, and 0.85 denote Dice agreement between perturbed and original masks, not percentages of labels corrupted. Five runs per architecture and perturbation pair are reported, but Table 1 provides no uncertainty. Boundary-perturbation results were explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they do not require missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labeling, training error, and chance-level test error.
Training time and convergence as label corruption increases.

Whether training error stays perfect; corruption rates through fully random labels; whether test error approaches chance. Only test Dice at random perturbation settings tuned to 0.95, 0.90, and 0.85 agreement is reported.
Weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, and their effects on random-label fitting or true-label generalization.
Order of learning real-data patterns and memorizing noisy labels.

tranche.reason: Tests the test-performance component of V4 in a new setting: liver segmentation with randomly corrupted voxel masks and clean evaluation annotations.
